title: Contract-backed capacity enforcer with graceful degradation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement an autoscaling policy engine component that enforces contract-level throughput guarantees while minimizing cost and preserving reliability. The enforcer maps a customer's committed throughput contract into per-tenant scaling budgets and admission controls. It should provide graceful degradation when capacity is constrained: prioritized request routing, soft-fail fallbacks to lower-cost model variants, and explicit user-facing signals for contract breach events. The component lives in Dedicated capacity control plane and interacts with the existing scaling orchestrator, the quota accounting service, and the runtime admission layer.
acceptance_criteria: Simulated 30-day workload with mixed burstiness: 99.95% of committed throughput delivered within contracted latency SLOs in lab simulations
Maximum fleet overshoot limited to 1.4x committed headroom during a 15m surge in stress tests
Scaling decisions never ramp up more than 2x capacity in a single 60s window (ramp-rate safety limit)
Fallback chain (same-model-slim, quantized-variant, fallback-model) triggered deterministically and logged with reason codes
End-to-end integration tests with dedicated autoscaler, admission control, and billing show correct charge attribution for contract enforcement
Operational metrics emitted: contract_violation_count, enforced_capacity, grace_throttle_pct, fallback_invocations — appear in Console dashboards
design_notes: Key ideas: 1) Convert contract throughput (requests/min or tokens/sec) into a dynamic target reserve expressed as 'committed tokens per minute' and maintain a sliding credit bucket per tenant. 2) Use EWMA-smoothed observed demand plus a quantile headroom (e.g., 95th percentile of recent per-minute demand) to set transient scale targets. 3) Apply a three-tier safety envelope: absolute max replicas, per-minute ramp rate, and rolling cooldowns after scale events. 4) Admission layer consults the enforcer and returns either go/queue/soft-fail with an ordered fallback. 5) Billing hooks mark excess consumption above committed throughput for overage pricing and emit audit events.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Spec and simulator (2 sprints) — finalize math for credit buckets, EWMA parameters, and safety envelope constants. Phase 2: Prototype enforcer service + admission hook (3 sprints) — implement stateful per-tenant credit accounting, integrate with scaling orchestrator reconciliation loop. Phase 3: Canary on small Dedicated fleet (2 weeks) — run synthetic workloads, chaos tests, and observe Console metrics. Phase 4: Rollout and docs (1 sprint) — add operator runbook, alerting thresholds, and public docs for customers.
tradeoffs_and_risks: - Overly conservative safety limits increase latency for customers with bursty traffic. - Aggressive ramping may cause cost overruns and noisy neighbor effects on shared pools. - Stateful per-tenant buckets increase control-plane state; we must bound memory and use efficient eviction. - Complexity of fallback chains requires careful monitoring to avoid silent quality regressions.
alternatives_considered: Pure reactive autoscaling based solely on instantaneous concurrency — rejected because it cannot honor committed throughput guarantees during rapid bursts
Global headroom pooling (shared buffer across tenants) — considered but poses fairness and billing complexity for contract-backed guarantees
ML-based demand predictor — deferred to future work; chosen approach uses lightweight EWMA + percentile to keep behavior interpretable and debuggable
testing_plan: Unit tests for credit bucket semantics, rate-limiter integration, and fallback decision matrix
Large-scale simulator validating policy behavior across synthetic traces (steady, diurnal, spiky, and power-law bursts)
Integration tests linking enforcer -> autoscaler -> runtime admission with canary traffic
Chaos test: induce partial capacity failures and validate graceful degradation and rollback behavior
Performance benchmark: ensure enforcer decision latency < 15ms at 10k tenants
observability_and_alerting: Emit time-series for enforced_capacity, requested_capacity, contract_usage_pct, grace_throttle_pct, fallback_invocations. Add alerts for contract_violation_rate > 0.1% over 10m, enforcer_error_rate > 0.1%, and exceeding ramp-rate thresholds. Create dashboard in Console under 'Dedicated / Autoscaling / Contract Enforcement'.
open_questions: What should the default percentile headroom be for new customers (95th vs 99th)?
Do we allow tenant-level overrides for ramp-rate and max_replicas in admin UI?
How to reconcile multi-tenant shared buffer policy with per-tenant contractual isolation when a fleet is near capacity?
